title: Kids Martial Arts Software: Family Accounts (2026)
description: Software for kids martial arts programs: one parent login for siblings, family billing and guardian waivers compared across 7 tools, with prices.
h1: Software for kids martial arts programs
body:
In most karate, taekwondo and BJJ schools the kids program pays the bills, and kids programs come with parents. The parent is the one who books, pays, signs the waiver and reads your messages, and often two or three siblings train at once. So the software questions are different from an adult gym: can one parent log in for every child, can you bill a household with a sibling discount, and will the system collect a guardian's signature for a minor?

We checked seven martial arts tools against those three questions on November 15, 2026, using only each vendor's own pages and help-center articles. Anything a vendor doesn't publish is marked unknown. We have not used these tools ourselves and we don't publish ratings.

What each tool publishes for kids programs

  • Gymdesk documents the most complete family setup of the tools we checked. A family account shares one payment method on the primary member, can send all invoices and reminders to that member's email, and lets the primary update every child's details, including from the member app. You can price a family-shared membership by the number of active family members, or give per-child memberships a "3rd family member" style discount, and a setting auto-adjusts family discounts. Waivers can require a guardian signature for anyone under the minor age you set. Its BJJ features post also lists separate kids age brackets and belt systems. {{aff:gymdesk|See Gymdesk pricing}}
  • Zen Planner links a family under a Head of Household. Memberships bill to the same payment method, on one transaction when the bill dates line up. Its help center recommends a separate membership per child (for example $120 for the first and $100 for a "+1" sibling) so one child can cancel without touching the others. If you turn on "Ask If Guardian?", a parent can register a child online and signs the waiver for the child and for themselves. Parents then switch between children in the Member App. One catch from the help center: discounts set up under Fees & Discounts can't be applied to sales made in the Staff App or Front Desk. {{aff:zenplanner|See Zen Planner pricing}}
  • Spark Membership keeps siblings under one family account that's billed and messaged together, while each child keeps their own rank history, attendance and signed waiver. One parent login in the free Spark Member App can book, check in and pay for each child, and kids, teen and adult programs can each follow their own rank order. Spark is $199/mo after an 8-week trial.
  • PushPress puts each child on their own profile and membership under the parent's account, so the parent pays for everyone, and says family memberships can be discounted. Waivers can be signed by a parent online when booking the first class or on the front-desk tablet. Belt tests run as invite-only events with a testing fee, and birthday parties and summer camps run as events too. Note that belt tracking is on Pro ($159/mo) and Max ($229/mo), not the Free plan.
  • Kicksite groups students and non-training contacts into Families with a Primary, usually a parent. A card added to the family profile works for every member, and the Primary can see every family member in the Member Portal. Payments are applied to one profile at a time, so you can't pay the whole family's open balance in a single payment. A Family Management Form lets parents update their own contact details.
  • Martialytics lists family accounts with one payer and several students, plus family discounts. For the Student Portal, each child is invited separately; the parent accepts every invite with the same email and password, then picks a child when booking. Its One Touch Sign-Up form collects details, billing and waiver signatures in one go. {{aff:martialytics|See Martialytics plans}}
  • MatGoat lets a parent who doesn't train manage linked children, and a child can have a managed profile with no email address. Family pricing is a set of total-price tiers by number of children on one plan; the top tier also applies to larger families. Online collection needs payment management, which is on Professional ($60/mo).

How to test a kids program setup on a free trial

  1. Build your hardest family. One parent, two kids in different programs (say Little Dragons and Juniors), one sibling discount. See whether you need one membership per child or one shared family membership, and what happens when one child quits.
  2. Log in as the parent. Book a class for one child, check in the other, and update the card. Count the logins it takes.
  3. Sign a waiver as a guardian for a child under your state's age of majority, and check where the signed copy is stored.
  4. Promote a child. Kids belt systems often use stripes or tips between belts. Check that kids and adults can follow separate rank orders; see our belt rank tracking software guide.
  5. Price the whole household. Per-student pricing (Kicksite, Martialytics, Gymdesk, Zen Planner) means every sibling counts toward your tier. Our martial arts software pricing guide shows cost by student count.

faq: What is the best software for a kids martial arts program?

No single tool wins on published data. As of November 15, 2026, Gymdesk documents the most complete family setup we found (shared payment method, family-size pricing or sibling discounts, and a required guardian signature for minors), from $75/mo with Gymdesk Payments. Zen Planner, Spark Membership and PushPress also document one parent login for several children plus family billing.
Which martial arts software lets one parent manage several kids?

Gymdesk, Zen Planner, Spark Membership, PushPress, Kicksite (the family Primary), Martialytics (one Student Portal login per shared email) and MatGoat (a parent or representative manages linked children) all describe this on their own pages or help centers (checked 2026-11-15).
Can martial arts software give sibling discounts automatically?

Gymdesk can price a family-shared membership by number of family members or apply an nth-family-member discount, with a setting to auto-adjust family discounts. MatGoat uses total-price tiers by number of children. Zen Planner, PushPress and Martialytics also describe family discounts; Kicksite's family docs we read don't mention sibling discounts.
Which tools collect a guardian signature on a minor's waiver?

Gymdesk (a setting requires a guardian signature under the minor age you choose), Zen Planner (with "Ask If Guardian?" on, the guardian signs for the child and for themselves) and PushPress (parent and guardian signatures for minors) say so on their own pages. Spark keeps a signed waiver on each child's profile. We didn't find guardian-signing details for Martialytics, Kicksite or MatGoat.
Do siblings count toward per-student pricing?

Usually yes: Kicksite, Martialytics and Zen Planner price by active students or members, and Gymdesk by active members, so each enrolled child counts toward your tier. PushPress plans have unlimited students, MatGoat Professional is unlimited, and Spark publishes a single $199/mo price.
